- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).

# Tooltip contents stop refreshing while it stays open

**Describe the bug**
Hovering the bar in the screenshot pops the tooltip captured there. Everything it shows is fed by
values that keep moving while the panel is on screen — the readout on its first line, the label on
its second, and its own highlight, which is meant to switch over to the "reached" treatment the
moment the point it describes is reached.

Instead the whole tooltip locks to however it looked the instant it appeared. Both lines sit there
unchanged and the highlight never switches over, for as long as it stays open, while every other
figure on the panel behind it keeps ticking over. Moving away and hovering again is the only way to
get current contents.

Sliding straight from one point on the bar to the next must still show the values for the one
actually under the cursor, without waiting.

**Screenshots**
![bug screenshot](/app/.harbor_assets/bug.png)

None of its vocabulary appears anywhere near the responsible source: the only route to the code is reading the poster. The screenshot carries the localizing evidence — the cycling rift name rendered mid-scramble ('çaAuIm', a shifted state of the Vacuum rift's name list), the '... also affects EP gain' milestone text, the 'Drains IP to fill.' panel copy and the '63.449% (Idle)' bar readout — and those visible strings are what lead to the celestial-pelle rift bar and its milestone hover tooltip. Text-only search for the instruction's own wording ('refreshing', 'readout', 'locks to', 'marker') resolves to nothing in that directory, so the defect cannot be localized without the pixels.
19	
20	The fix itself is non-trivial Vue 2 reasoning, and the obvious one-liner is not enough. The tooltip body is a v-slot template handed to CustomizeableTooltip, which Vue 2.6 compiles as a STABLE scoped slot: the slot function runs during the child's render, so the parent re-rendering every tick does not refresh it, and a parent-level $forceUpdate() does not either. The only thing that refreshes it is a reactive value, read inside the slot, actually changing — and on base every one of the three things the tooltip renders comes from a source Vue cannot track. The description is a getter that re-runs a word-cycling function on each read; the resource line calls rift.config.percentageToFill(); and the highlight comes from the tooltipContentStyle computed, which reads the milestone's canBeApplied — a PROTOTYPE getter on RiftMilestoneState/GameMechanicState derived from live game state. Vue's observer only converts own enumerable properties, so canBeApplied never becomes a dependency and that computed's cache is never invalidated. Nothing ever invalidates the slot, so both text lines AND the highlight freeze at whatever first rendered.
21	
22	That third surface is the part a shallow fix misses. The upstream PR itself only cached the two text lines, so reproducing it verbatim leaves the highlight frozen and scores 0.5. Getting to 1.0 means recognising that a computed reading an untracked prototype getter is stale for the same reason the template method calls are, and routing all three through state written on the update() tick the codebase already uses. There is a second trap in the other direction: caching purely on the tick regresses hovering, because sliding onto a new milestone then shows the previous milestone's values until the next tick — a p2p that passes on base guards that, so a tick-only cache also fails.
23	
24	The verifier mounts the real component together with the real CustomizeableTooltip (SFC templates compiled inside the harness), drives the tick by calling update() exactly as GameUI does, drives hovering through the component's own mousemove handler, and asserts only rendered output — the highlight check compares rendered markup with both text lines held constant, so it pins no colour, class or style property. Any architecture passes: a reactive data cache under any property name, computed properties keyed off a tick counter, a watcher, or a fix living in the tooltip component instead."""

FROM node:18-bookworm

RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    git \
    ca-certificates \
    python3 \
 && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

WORKDIR /app

# Clone the repository, pin to the base commit, then strip .git so the agent
# cannot inspect the fix PR or future history (anti-cheat). Re-init a single
# base commit with an immutable tag so the verifier can reset test files and
# git apply still works without upstream history.
RUN git clone https://github.com/IvarK/AntimatterDimensionsSourceCode /app \
 && git -C /app checkout b07bff4ec0ded834890fce6cff4af8555b9f68a9 \
 && rm -rf /app/.git \
 && git -C /app init -q \
 && git -C /app -c user.email=h@l -c user.name=h add -A \
 && git -C /app -c user.email=h@l -c user.name=h commit -q -m base \
 && git -C /app tag harbor_base

# Pre-install repo dependencies so verify time doesn't wait on the network.
# Use npm ci for reproducible install from the lockfile.
RUN npm ci --prefer-offline 2>/dev/null || npm install --legacy-peer-deps

# Visual evidence, readable by the agent at /app/.harbor_assets/.
# tests/ and solution/ are intentionally NOT copied into the image —
# the harness supplies them at verify time.
RUN mkdir -p /logs /app/.harbor_assets
COPY assets/ /app/.harbor_assets/

CMD ["bash"]

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Behavioral verifier for ivark__antimatterdimensionssourcecode-2808-mm
3	#
4	# The milestone hover tooltip on the celestial-pelle rift bar freezes at its
5	# first-rendered contents: both of its lines are produced by template method
6	# calls inside a stable scoped slot, so nothing invalidates the slot when the
7	# underlying (non-reactive) values advance.
8	#
9	# NEVER greps candidate source, and asserts no property/function/file name. The
10	# real component is mounted together with the real CustomizeableTooltip in jsdom,
11	# the game tick is driven by calling update() the way GameUI does, and only the
12	# RENDERED tooltip text is asserted across ticks — so any fix that actually makes
13	# the tooltip track its sources passes, whatever its shape or location.
14	#
15	# Synthetic test: repo has no test framework; jest + custom vue-script-transformer
16	# (uses @babel/core already in devDeps) added via test.patch for this eval only.
17	
18	set -uo pipefail
19	
20	mkdir -p /logs/verifier
21	
22	STDOUT_LOG=/logs/verifier/test-stdout.txt
23	STDERR_LOG=/logs/verifier/test-stderr.txt
24	REPORT=/logs/verifier/jest-results.json
25	
26	: > "$STDOUT_LOG"
27	: > "$STDERR_LOG"
28	
29	ensure_reward() {
30	  [ -f /logs/verifier/reward.txt ] || echo 0 > /logs/verifier/reward.txt
31	}
32	trap ensure_reward EXIT
33	
34	cd /app || { echo "no /app" | tee -a "$STDERR_LOG"; exit 1; }
35	
36	# ── Step 1: Reset test.patch paths from harbor_base ────────────────────────────
37	# Extract EVERY path from diff --git headers (text, binary, renamed, deleted).
38	# Restore each to pristine base state so the apply is idempotent and any agent
39	# edits to those paths cannot influence scoring.
40	_patch_paths=$(
41	  { sed -n 's#^diff --git a/\(.*\) b/.*#\1#p' /tests/test.patch
42	    sed -n 's#^diff --git a/.* b/\(.*\)#\1#p' /tests/test.patch
43	  } | sort -u )
44	
45	for _p in $_patch_paths; do
46	  git -C /app checkout harbor_base -- "$_p" 2>/dev/null \
47	    || rm -f "/app/$_p" 2>/dev/null \
48	    || true
49	done
50	git -C /app clean -fdq -- $(
51	  printf '%s\n' $_patch_paths | xargs -r -n1 dirname | sort -u
52	) 2>/dev/null || true
53	
54	# ── Step 2: Apply test.patch ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
55	echo "== applying test.patch ==" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
56	git apply /tests/test.patch 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" \
57	  || patch -p1 -i /tests/test.patch 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" \
58	  || { echo "ERROR: could not apply test.patch" | tee -a "$STDERR_LOG"; exit 1; }
59	
60	# ── Step 3: Install pinned test-only deps ─────────────────────────────────────
61	# Do NOT modify package.json / package-lock.json (--no-save --no-package-lock).
62	#
63	# jest@27.5.1         — test runner; bundles jest-environment-jsdom
64	# babel-jest@27.5.1   — transforms .js test files (ES module → CJS for Node)
65	# @babel/preset-env@7 — used by both babel-jest (test file) and the custom
66	#                       vue-script-transformer.js (component script block)
67	#
68	# @babel/core and vue-template-compiler are already in node_modules (npm ci).
69	# vue-jest is NOT installed here — the custom vue-script-transformer.js avoids
70	# the vue-jest@4/jest@27 getCacheKey API incompatibility.
71	echo "== installing pinned test-only deps ==" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
72	npm install --no-save --no-package-lock --legacy-peer-deps \
73	  jest@27.5.1 \
74	  babel-jest@27.5.1 \
75	  "@babel/preset-env@7.23.5" \
76	  >>"$STDOUT_LOG" 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" \
77	  || { echo "ERROR: npm install for test deps failed" | tee -a "$STDERR_LOG"; exit 1; }
78	
79	# ── Step 4: Run the synthetic reactivity spec ──────────────────────────────────
80	# --json --outputFile: produce machine-readable report for verifier.py.
81	# jest exits non-zero on test failure; capture code, don't abort.
82	echo "== running f2p test ==" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
83	npx jest \
84	  --config /app/jest.config.js \
85	  --json \
86	  --outputFile "$REPORT" \
87	  --testPathPattern="PelleRiftBar.reactivity.spec.js" \
88	  --no-coverage \
89	  >>"$STDOUT_LOG" 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" \
90	  || echo "(jest exited non-zero; parsing report for reward)" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Behavioral verifier for ivark__antimatterdimensionssourcecode-2808-mm
#
# The milestone hover tooltip on the celestial-pelle rift bar freezes at its
# first-rendered contents: both of its lines are produced by template method
# calls inside a stable scoped slot, so nothing invalidates the slot when the
# underlying (non-reactive) values advance.
#
# NEVER greps candidate source, and asserts no property/function/file name. The
# real component is mounted together with the real CustomizeableTooltip in jsdom,
# the game tick is driven by calling update() the way GameUI does, and only the
# RENDERED tooltip text is asserted across ticks — so any fix that actually makes
# the tooltip track its sources passes, whatever its shape or location.
#
# Synthetic test: repo has no test framework; jest + custom vue-script-transformer
# (uses @babel/core already in devDeps) added via test.patch for this eval only.

set -uo pipefail

mkdir -p /logs/verifier

STDOUT_LOG=/logs/verifier/test-stdout.txt
STDERR_LOG=/logs/verifier/test-stderr.txt
REPORT=/logs/verifier/jest-results.json

: > "$STDOUT_LOG"
: > "$STDERR_LOG"

ensure_reward() {
  [ -f /logs/verifier/reward.txt ] || echo 0 > /logs/verifier/reward.txt
}
trap ensure_reward EXIT

cd /app || { echo "no /app" | tee -a "$STDERR_LOG"; exit 1; }

# ── Step 1: Reset test.patch paths from harbor_base ────────────────────────────
# Extract EVERY path from diff --git headers (text, binary, renamed, deleted).
# Restore each to pristine base state so the apply is idempotent and any agent
# edits to those paths cannot influence scoring.
_patch_paths=$(
  { sed -n 's#^diff --git a/\(.*\) b/.*#\1#p' /tests/test.patch
    sed -n 's#^diff --git a/.* b/\(.*\)#\1#p' /tests/test.patch
  } | sort -u )

for _p in $_patch_paths; do
  git -C /app checkout harbor_base -- "$_p" 2>/dev/null \
    || rm -f "/app/$_p" 2>/dev/null \
    || true
done
git -C /app clean -fdq -- $(
  printf '%s\n' $_patch_paths | xargs -r -n1 dirname | sort -u
) 2>/dev/null || true

# ── Step 2: Apply test.patch ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
echo "== applying test.patch ==" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
git apply /tests/test.patch 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" \
  || patch -p1 -i /tests/test.patch 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" \
  || { echo "ERROR: could not apply test.patch" | tee -a "$STDERR_LOG"; exit 1; }

# ── Step 3: Install pinned test-only deps ─────────────────────────────────────
# Do NOT modify package.json / package-lock.json (--no-save --no-package-lock).
#
# jest@27.5.1         — test runner; bundles jest-environment-jsdom
# babel-jest@27.5.1   — transforms .js test files (ES module → CJS for Node)
# @babel/preset-env@7 — used by both babel-jest (test file) and the custom
#                       vue-script-transformer.js (component script block)
#
# @babel/core and vue-template-compiler are already in node_modules (npm ci).
# vue-jest is NOT installed here — the custom vue-script-transformer.js avoids
# the vue-jest@4/jest@27 getCacheKey API incompatibility.
echo "== installing pinned test-only deps ==" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
npm install --no-save --no-package-lock --legacy-peer-deps \
  jest@27.5.1 \
  babel-jest@27.5.1 \
  "@babel/preset-env@7.23.5" \
  >>"$STDOUT_LOG" 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" \
  || { echo "ERROR: npm install for test deps failed" | tee -a "$STDERR_LOG"; exit 1; }

# ── Step 4: Run the synthetic reactivity spec ──────────────────────────────────
# --json --outputFile: produce machine-readable report for verifier.py.
# jest exits non-zero on test failure; capture code, don't abort.
echo "== running f2p test ==" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
npx jest \
  --config /app/jest.config.js \
  --json \
  --outputFile "$REPORT" \
  --testPathPattern="PelleRiftBar.reactivity.spec.js" \
  --no-coverage \
  >>"$STDOUT_LOG" 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" \
  || echo "(jest exited non-zero; parsing report for reward)" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"

echo "== computing reward ==" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
python3 /tests/verifier.py 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
echo "reward=$(cat /logs/verifier/reward.txt 2>/dev/null)" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""
3	Verifier for ivark__antimatterdimensionssourcecode-2808-mm
4	Parses the jest --json report and computes the SWE-bench-style reward.
5	
6	Jest JSON schema (relevant for individual test access):
7	  {
8	    "testResults": [            ← array of test SUITES (one per .spec.js file)
9	      {
10	        "assertionResults": [   ← individual test cases (NOT "testResults"!)
11	          { "fullName": "...", "status": "passed" | "failed" | "pending" }
12	        ],
13	        "status": "passed" | "failed"
14	      }
15	    ]
16	  }
17	
18	Reward policy:
19	  1.0 — every f2p test passes AND every p2p test passes (p2p vacuously true if [])
20	  0.5 — f2p partially passes OR f2p all pass but a p2p regressed
21	  0.0 — no f2p test passes, or report is missing / unparseable
22	
23	CRITICAL: this script MUST write the reward to /logs/verifier/reward.txt.
24	Harbor reads that file; a print-only script yields RewardFileNotFoundError.
25	"""
26	import json
27	import os
28	import re
29	import sys
30	
31	CONF_PATH = "/tests/config.json"
32	REPORT_PATH = "/logs/verifier/jest-results.json"
33	REWARD_PATH = "/logs/verifier/reward.txt"
34	
35	
36	def load_config():
37	    with open(CONF_PATH) as fh:
38	        return json.load(fh)
39	
40	
41	def load_results():
42	    """
43	    Parse jest's --json output and return a flat dict:
44	        { test_full_name: "pass" | "fail" | "skip" }
45	
46	    Jest JSON schema (assertionResults, not testResults, for individual tests):
47	      {
48	        "testResults": [                     <- suites
49	          {
50	            "assertionResults": [            <- individual tests
51	              { "fullName": "...", "status": "passed"|"failed"|"pending" }
52	            ]
53	          }
54	        ]
55	      }
56	    """
57	    results = {}
58	    if not os.path.exists(REPORT_PATH):
59	        print(f"[verifier] WARNING: report not found at {REPORT_PATH}", file=sys.stderr)
60	        return results
61	
62	    try:
63	        data = json.load(open(REPORT_PATH))
64	    except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
65	        print(f"[verifier] ERROR: cannot parse report JSON: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
66	        return results
67	
68	    for suite in data.get("testResults", []):
69	        # Jest uses "assertionResults" for individual test cases within a suite.
70	        for tc in suite.get("assertionResults", []):
71	            name = tc.get("fullName", tc.get("title", ""))
72	            status = tc.get("status", "unknown")
73	            if status == "passed":
74	                results[name] = "pass"
75	            elif status == "pending":
76	                results[name] = "skip"
77	            else:
78	                results[name] = "fail"
79	
80	    return results
81	
82	
83	def match_ident(ident, results):
84	    """
85	    Match a configured test identifier against reported test names.
86	    Tries exact match first, then substring, then regex.
87	    Returns the status string or "missing".
88	    """
89	    if ident in results:
90	        return results[ident]
91	    hit = next((v for k, v in results.items() if ident in k), None)
92	    if hit is not None:
93	        return hit
94	    try:
95	        hit = next((v for k, v in results.items() if re.search(re.escape(ident), k)), None)
96	    except re.error:
97	        hit = None
98	    return hit if hit is not None else "missing"
99	
100	
101	def main():
102	    conf = load_config()
103	    f2p_ids = conf.get("f2p", [])
104	    p2p_ids = conf.get("p2p", [])
105	
106	    results = load_results()
107	
108	    f2p_map = {ident: match_ident(ident, results) for ident in f2p_ids}
109	    p2p_map = {ident: match_ident(ident, results) for ident in p2p_ids}
110	
111	    f2p_passed = [k for k, v in f2p_map.items() if v == "pass"]
112	    p2p_passed = [k for k, v in p2p_map.items() if v == "pass"]
113	
114	    all_f2p = len(f2p_passed) == len(f2p_ids) and len(f2p_ids) > 0
115	    all_p2p = len(p2p_passed) == len(p2p_ids)  # vacuously true if p2p is []
116	
117	    if all_f2p and all_p2p:
118	        reward = 1.0
119	    elif f2p_passed and (not all_p2p or not all_f2p):
120	        reward = 0.5
121	    else:
122	        reward = 0.0
123	
124	    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(REWARD_PATH), exist_ok=True)
125	    with open(REWARD_PATH, "w") as fh:
126	        fh.write(str(reward))
127	
128	    report = {
129	        "reward": reward,
130	        "f2p": f2p_map,
131	        "p2p": p2p_map,
132	        "f2p_passed_count": len(f2p_passed),
133	        "f2p_total": len(f2p_ids),
134	        "p2p_passed_count": len(p2p_passed),
135	        "p2p_total": len(p2p_ids),
136	    }
137	    print(json.dumps(report, indent=2))
138	
139	
140	if __name__ == "__main__":
141	    main()
